text:
emma: FYI seeing a burst of 503s from hosted inference for a handful of customers. root cause looks like upstream inference workers getting killed by the watchdog in a hotloop.

devon: Can you paste the pod/runner exit reason? OOM, segfault, or SIGKILL?

emma: quick paste from one affected node: 
```
[2026-03-16T21:03:05Z] infer-runner[pid=4123] watchdog: terminating process after 30s stall
[2026-03-16T21:03:05Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4123 (infer-runner) total-vm:1234564kB
[2026-03-16T21:03:05Z] containerd: infer-runner exited with status 137
```
Looks like OOM kills, but the timing is odd — many pods restarted almost simultaneously.

miguel_sre: Heap/host memory or GPU oom? Need `nvidia-smi` from the node and container logs. Also which model and batchsize were running?

emma: Model: rw-ggml-7b-quant (hosted variant). Batchsize autoset to 8 by runtime for high qps. `nvidia-smi` snapshot: 
```
GPU 0  31%  Mem:  15616MiB / 16384MiB
GPU 1  95%  Mem:  16352MiB / 16384MiB  (runner processes listed pinned to GPU1)
```
Multiple runners on same host pinned to GPU1 due to scheduling; when one OOMed the watchdog killed it and kubelet rescheduled other runners which caused an eviction cascade.

lina_support: Customers A & B reported 503s starting ~21:03 UTC, about 2m impact, several timed-out retries causing billing duplications in logs. CS opened tickets. Any quick mitigations?

autoscale-bot: [21:04:12] cluster-autoscaler: scale-down inhibited for node/node-12 due to recent pod evictions.
autoscale-bot: [21:04:17] cluster-autoscaler: attempt to remove node/node-12 failed (pods pending).

devon: Root cause seems like scheduling packup: multiple high-memory runners ended up on the same GPU. When one process hits OOM it frees memory then kubelet restarts another that may try to grab the same memory, causing a tight restart loop — watchdog keeps killing perceived hung processes. Two-prong mitigation: 1) immediate routing fallback to lower-memory model variant or CPU fallback for affected customers; 2) short-term admission control to cap batchsize and concurrency on that host.

miguel_sre: Agreed. Also suggests changing the watchdog threshold to be less aggressive for 10m, while we stabilize scheduling. Workaround commands: 
```
# patch runtime admission to limit per-runner concurrency
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/overrides -d '{"selector":"host:node-12","max_inflight":2}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# route customers with high error rate to rw-ggml-3b-quant temporarily
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/route -d '{"customer":"acme","model":"rw-ggml-3b-quant","weight":100}'
```

emma: I patched a routing override to move two high-QPS customers to the 3b variant and lowered max_inflight on node-12. Error rate dropped within 40s.

lina_support: Noted. CS updated tickets and issued credit hold for impacted calls. Please confirm follow-up timeline for root cause fix.

devon: Next steps I propose: 
- repro locally with constrained GPU memory and many runners pinned to same device (use `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` on multi-runner test harness).
- adjust scheduler GPU-affinity rules to enforce spread (binpack -> spread policy for high-mem models).
- change watchdog heuristic to consider OOM exit codes (137) and backoff restarts for 30s instead of immediate kill-loop.

miguel_sre: Adding notes: observed exit code 137 consistently; no coredump or segfault. Kernel OOM (oom_score) bumped for `infer-runner` at kill time. Suggest debottlenecking by: 
- Q1: scheduler anti-colocation for models with >14GB memory footprint.
- Q1: autoscaler policy to avoid simultaneous scale-in during high-restart windows.
- Q2: runtime admission control to cap batching based on real-time memory telemetry.

emma: I'll file infra tickets and tag oncall for scheduler change. Short-term: revert aggressive scale-down to prevent churn.

devon: For repro steps I'll attach a tiny test harness: 
```
# quick repro (dev env)
for i in {1..6}; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 ./runner --model rw-ggml-7b-quant --max-batch 8 & done
# generate long-context calls to fill KV cache and force memory pressure
python3 tools/loadgen.py --qps 50 --ctx-len 1024 --duration 120
```

lina_support: CS asks for ETA on full mitigation and whether customers should expect any more credits. Also asked if we should proactively route other customers during fix window.

emma: ETA: patching scheduler and autoscaler policy tomorrow morning (PST). I'll send an incident follow-up doc with timeline and impacted customers. For now we've routed the highest QPS customers off the affected nodes and increased backoff on watchdog.

miguel_sre: I'll follow up with a PR for scheduler spread and a config change for the watchdog (increase backoff and classify 137 as OOM->backoff).

devon: Also adding a monitoring alert: detect >3 distinct runner restarts on same GPU within 5m and trigger automated routing to lower-memory variants.

lina_support: Thanks all, CS will monitor open tickets and update customers. :thumbsup:

autoscale-bot: [21:23:07] cluster-autoscaler: scaled up node/node-14 to relieve load on node-12.

emma: closing thread here; will link incident postmortem when created.
